chunks: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “Indeed, in al-Fiṭr there is takbīr, but it is a recommended sunnah.”

He said: I said, “Then where is it?” He said: “On the night of al-Fiṭr, in al-Maghrib and the later ʿIshāʾ, and in salat al-Fajr and in salat al-ʿĪd.” And in a narration other than that of Saʿīd: “And in al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr, then it stops.”

He said: I said, “How shall I say it?” He said: “You say: Allah is greater, Allah is greater, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greater, Allah is greater, and to Allah belongs all praise. Allah is greater for what He has guided us to, and all praise belongs to Allah for what He has tried us with.”
And this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And that you complete the number” meaning the fasting, “and that you magnify Allah for what He has guided you to.”

key_terms.الْعِدَّةَ: the prescribed number or period, explained here as the fasting period
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: ʿĪd al-Fiṭr, the occasion marking the end of fasting
key_terms.تَكْبِيرًا: the declaration of Allah’s greatness recited on the occasion
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْعِيدِ: the ʿĪd prayer associated with this takbīr
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer in which this takbīr is recited
key_terms.هَدَاكُمْ: guided you, referring to Allah’s guidance for which He is magnified

ai.seo_question: What is the takbīr of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr, when is it recited, and what wording should be said?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the takbīr of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr is a recommended sunnah and specifies the prayers in which it is recited. It also gives the wording of the takbīr and links the practice to the Qur’anic command to complete the fasting period and magnify Allah for His guidance.
